_readme: Copy this file to scope.json in the engagement folder and fill every empty field.
Take every value from the written authorization. The operator confirms the file before any testing.
Validate it with: python3 scripts/scope_check.py --scope scope.json --validate
Keys that start with an underscore are comments. Any other unknown key is an error.
A host name such as example.com covers that name only. *.example.com covers every name under it, but not example.com itself. This holds for both lists.
Host names are never resolved by the checker. Resolved addresses must be in ip_ranges to be in scope.
Run scripts/scope_check.py --list-techniques to see the technique classes.

authorization._help: Who authorized the testing, and where the written authorization is kept (document title, ticket or contract reference).

window._help: ISO 8601 with a time zone, for example 2030-01-07T09:00:00+00:00. Testing is allowed from start up to, but not including, end.

techniques._help: A class must be in allowed and absent from forbidden. The six classes below are refused by the checker in every case. They are listed so the file states it plainly.

data_handling._help: Edit the rules to match the authorization. retention says how long evidence is kept and how it is disposed of.
rules: Collect the minimum evidence needed to prove each finding.
Do not open, copy or keep personal data or third-party data. Stop and report if it is encountered.
Redact passwords, keys and tokens in evidence and reports.
Keep all evidence inside the engagement folder.

stop_conditions: A target turns out to be outside the scope or owned by someone else.
Any sign of impact on a production service.
Personal data or third-party data is encountered.
The authorization is unclear or disputed.

emergency_contact._help: Someone who can be reached during the testing window and can stop the test.

hardware.description: lab router on the test bench
hardware.restore_image_sha256: <SHA-256 of a restore image that was verified to work>
